races.title: State Assembly, District 46
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jesse Gabriel
cands.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the western San Fernando Valley, first elected in a 2018 special election. Chairs the Assembly Budget Committee. Former Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher litigator and counsel to U.S. Sen. Evan Bayh. Harvard Law and UC Berkeley graduate.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, and YIMBY Action.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position from Gabriel on data centers or on new development or growth limits. We found nothing on homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties. His birth date and place come from Wikipedia alone. The Ballotpedia page said he skipped its 2026 candidate survey, so his own 2026 statements are limited to his campaign site.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Berkeley and raised in Oak Park, California; Ballotpedia says he graduated from Oak Park High School in 2000 and now lives in Encino.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the California Assembly since 2018 and chairs the Budget Committee. Earlier he was an Assistant Majority Whip, counsel to a U.S. senator (2008-2010), and a litigator at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher.
qual.why: Eight years of legislative service and a leadership post (Assistant Majority Whip), plus legal and policy work in the U.S. Senate and private practice. The committee chair adds nothing to the score.
qual.label: Eight years of legislative service and a leadership post (Assistant Majority Whip), plus legal and policy work in the U.S. Senate and private practice. The committee chair adds nothing to the score.

second-amendment.evidence: Authored the 2023 Gun Violence Prevention and School Safety Act, which taxes gun industry profits to fund violence prevention and school safety; it was signed into law and opposed by the NRA and the California Rifle & Pistol Association.

pro-life.evidence: Was a principal co-author of the constitutional amendment to protect reproductive freedom in the California Constitution.

back-police-order.evidence: Introduced 2025 legislation strengthening penalties for looting and for impersonating first responders during wildfires and other emergencies; it was signed by the governor.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 3 backed by their record, 0 only promised

roots.summary: Wikipedia says he was born in Berkeley and raised in Oak Park, California; Ballotpedia says he graduated from Oak Park High School in 2000 and now lives in Encino.

cands.name: Tracey Schroeder
cands.bio: Los Angeles-born elementary school teacher who has taught with LAUSD since 1998. UCLA graduate with a master's from Phillips Graduate Institute. Ran for the LAUSD school board in 2022 and for California Assembly District 46 as a Republican in 2024 and 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for 2026 and 2024)
Reform California (listed among 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations)
Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and California Republican Assembly (self-reported in her 2024 Ballotpedia survey)

cands.gaps: We could not confirm where she grew up or whether she moved to California at some point. No independent news reporting about her was available. We found no documented stances from her on data centers, development or growth, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school vouchers. She has never held office, so there is no record of official actions.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia says she was born in Los Angeles, earned a UCLA degree in 1996, and has taught for LAUSD since 1998, and her campaign site calls her a '3rd generation valley girl'; where she grew up is not stated directly.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elementary school teacher with LAUSD since 1998 (about 25+ years, kindergarten through third grade); unsuccessful candidate for the LAUSD school board (2022) and Assembly (2024, 2026); no elected office or legislative, policy or budget career found.
qual.why: Her long teaching career is real-world work but is not directly related to writing law and the state budget, and she has held no elected office, so she falls in the low band.
qual.label: Her long teaching career is real-world work but is not directly related to writing law and the state budget, and she has held no elected office, so she falls in the low band.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site describes a grassroots campaign with 'no corporate PAC money, no Sacramento insiders.'

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site says unlimited and unchecked taxation needs to end, that Proposition 13 must be protected, and that increased property taxes burden homeowners and renters. It does not mention a homestead exemption or ending home property taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site pledges to fund Prop 36 to ensure consequences for criminal behavior and to 'incentivize law enforcement'. In her 2024 survey she backed Prop 36 and repealing Prop 47.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In her 2022 LAUSD school board survey she said she would attract and retain staff through competitive salaries and benefits. She did not state a position on vouchers, charters or a specific raise.

prio.label: Matches 4 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 4 only promised

roots.summary: Ballotpedia says she was born in Los Angeles, earned a UCLA degree in 1996, and has taught for LAUSD since 1998, and her campaign site calls her a '3rd generation valley girl'; where she grew up is not stated directly.
